title: Media as marketing: why Corey Haines says to become the platform, not arbitrage it
summary: Corey explains his Swipe Files course on marketing like a media company. He contrasts arbitrage-era marketing with building content people return to, argues for owned distribution (newsletter, community), and says media personalities and company-wide buy-in are the real common thread.

principles.text: Keep shipping and putting stuff out there; consistent flailing builds mindshare, trust, network and opportunity.
principles.quote: it's this whole kind of Internet Serendipity you just have to ship you just have got to get stuff out there

principles.text: Don't play platform arbitrage (paid clicks, borrowed attention); become the platform yourself and monetize the attention you earn.
principles.quote: you essentially want to flip the model on its head and think about instead of trying to use a platform for Arbitrage how can I become the platform and then arbit triage it myself right

principles.text: Funnel social audiences back to owned distribution: newsletter, RSS, personal site, community or text list.
principles.quote: ideally you want everything to funnel back to an owned means of distribution which are really only a couple of things it's only a newsletter it's a RSS feed it's a personal website a community or a text mage list

principles.text: Media brands run on people: successful ones have recognizable personalities, and founders and teams should become them.
principles.quote: every big media brand usually has a couple of big media personalities behind them

principles.text: Public-facing employees multiply marketing reach, even when their job title isn't marketing.
principles.quote: you're building an army of marketers internally within the company even if their job title doesn't include marketing at all when they're sharing on social media when they're advocating for you

principles.text: A media-style strategy fails without top-down, culture-wide buy-in to the mission and long-term approach.
principles.quote: it has to be very like from a cultural level everyone's bought in everyone knows the idea everyone knows the mission
